cim: Google Cloud launches Gemini for Healthcare in preview
cim_eredeti: Google Cloud launches Gemini for Healthcare in preview
szoveg_eredeti:
Google Cloud has launched Gemini for Healthcare, a purpose-built agentic AI system now in preview for Gemini Enterprise customers. The system builds on the universal Gemini agent and unifies fragmented clinical, operational, and administrative workflows across provider and payer organisations.

Specialised skills guide agents through medical records synthesis and pre-appointment preparation. Further skills handle coverage and policy review alongside payer benefit determination. Teams can also build custom skills for workflows of their own, with human oversight built into every workflow and agents executing multi-step work inside defined guardrails.

Clinicians lose nearly 28 hours each week to clinical documentation and administrative requirements, according to a study from The Harris Poll and Google Cloud. That’s time drawn from care delivery and health plan operations. The burden fuels burnout experienced by 41.9 percent of physicians in a 2025 American Medical Association report on documentation pressure.

The American Hospital Association estimates administrative costs at 25 percent to 35 percent of total US healthcare spending. That share strains operating margins and leaves patients waiting longer for care, coverage decisions, and answers.

Thomas Kurian, CEO of Google Cloud, said: “The fundamental challenge in healthcare isn’t a lack of information – it’s the immense friction of making that data actionable across a highly regulated ecosystem.”

Direct integration with Epic runs through open.epic APIs, with Oracle Health connecting through Ignite APIs for FHIR. The secure read integration pulls active conditions, medications, and recent labs into the context agents reason across, without ever writing back to the EHR systems themselves. It’s a read-only approach the company says safeguards clinical data integrity.

InterSystems FHIR Server provides repository management and clinical data interoperability for standardised exchange across disparate care environments. Verato resolves patient identity across visits. Keragon extends connectivity to more than 400 healthcare applications, including EHRs and other healthcare systems, with connectivity for NextGen Healthcare remaining in development.

Governance applies across skills and connectors. Existing role-based access controls are preserved, with audit logging and verifiable citations giving clinical and IT leaders oversight. Responses are grounded in verified patient charts, approved guidelines, and evidence.

Patient records, prompts, and outputs remain within an organisation’s dedicated enterprise environment on Google Cloud; the company doesn’t use customer data to train foundation models, with HIPAA compliance supporting the whole architecture.

Payments and terminology networks support coding accuracy through lookups into CMS Coverage Data and the National Provider Identifier Registry, with RxNorm, ICD-10, and the IMO Health Knowledge Graph rounding out the terminology set.

Optum Network Eligibility and Coordination of Benefits, currently in limited release and testing, enables eligibility verification. Prior authorisation workflows run through Infinitus Relay, with Waystar and Cognizant Trizetto adding further revenue cycle integration and GoodRx contributing pricing data.

Clinicians can discover and cite peer-reviewed evidence through direct access to Optum EvidenceVue, ASCO guidelines, and BMJ Digital Health clinical decision support content, whether for treatment decisions or appeals.

Partner applications automate the surrounding workflows. Suki delivers Ambient Clinical Intelligence. UiPath automates clinical chart summaries and extracts citation-backed evidence, with Alteryx enabling automated analytics workflows and Synthpop automating back-office and patient-facing journey flows.

An integrated operational stack centralises communication across Google Workspace and Microsoft 365. ServiceNow and Salesforce’s agentic Health Cloud connect for cross-department coordination, with Sana from Workday streamlining enterprise knowledge and human resources workflows.

Check Point provides perimeter defence, with Cyera covering data and agent security. Together, the layers deliver protected health information context that supports HIPAA audits and compliance reporting.

The platform supports open model choice across Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI. Smart routing directs high-volume administrative tasks to fast low-cost models and reserves complex analysis for high-reasoning models.

Launch and testing customers include Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts, Hartford HealthCare, and HCA Healthcare. Highmark Health and Northwell Health are testing the preview alongside Optum and Stanford School of Medicine, with ASCO contributing guidelines content.
